a.text: Since the news, it's grown hard to put pen to paper.
I want to convey my grief, pain, anger, confusion, and I want to offer you consolation, all too late.
But the things you've said, and left unsaid, I understand equally. The despair that's driven you to sever all, to choose to give up on this life, that too I understand.
What else can I possibly write? All I could say, you surely already know.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Be strong, sir... this is all the first-aid I can give right now.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It'll be a little unbearable at first, but you'll be able to walk with enough effort. And if any Sarkaz come after you again, you'll be able to flee too.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Hahah. Thank you, madam...

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: I don't know who you are exactly, but I swear I've spotted you around before. You must be one of Lady Golding's like-minded friends.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Were you going to find her at the school? She's not with us anymore, exactly.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I know. Mm—I learned as much a while ago.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Please, save your strength. We need to leave this place as soon as we can. I fear that Sarkaz detachment will be back soon to sweep this area.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: So we've escaped. Now what?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Do you remember delivering a letter for Golding? Do you remember the distillery worker you contacted?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: If you're lost for any place to go, then seek him, and follow the trail from his place to flee the city.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I can't guarantee your safety; the line that intel came from is out of service by now. But if you do opt for it as a last resort, then you may ultimately find your way to some of the Self-Salvation Corps.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: No, or perhaps you'll find some... doctors. People similar enough to them, that is.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I'd wanted to seize on her letter as an opportunity, introduce her to the Doctor, to Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...In any case, go quickly. Each passing moment here is a moment in danger.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: And what about you?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You needn't worry about that. I have ways to hide myself.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: After all, there's plenty of ruins and rubble the Sarkaz have no interest in sweeping now, here in our grand old Londinium.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The Self-Salvation Corps will return, you know. Someone has to stay here to keep things prepared for them.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: That's wonderful, then. You know which way you should be going—so don't go sticking your neck out for me, now.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You mean—oh, don't say that, sir.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: I know, you know. Strange armies beyond the walls, and plenty chance of Sarkaz in any of the countless underground ways out.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: And where you plucked me free, that pile of rubble? That was my home... Hahah, I'm the same really. Yearning to see what isn't even there anymore.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Now's no time to lose heart. I've heard word of others, too, Self-Salvation Corps aside.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Sarkaz forces may be outside the city, but the dukes are about to formally enter their own troops into the fray. The blockades will soon be dusted aside, the Sarkaz will no longer seal the city entrance, and it'll be wide open again...

spans.text: Sarkaz forces may be outside the city, but the dukes are about to formally enter their
troops into the fray. The blockades will soon be dusted aside, the Sarkaz will no longer seal the city entrance, and it'll be wide open again...

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Thank you. But, well...

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: I can only imagine how well you knew Lady Golding.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: I only met her a scant few times, but I remember every time I took a letter from her hands, how gently she'd encourage me, just as you did now.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: And so, from time to time these days, I wonder...

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Why would someone like her choose to give up on her own life?

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Why, madam?

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Just walking takes some wind out of me, dragging my heavy leg. Could you go to the school for me and find an answer there?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Settle down, Leo!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: The Colonel may turn a blind eye for us, but the school is not safe anymore!

spans.text: The Colonel may turn a blind eye for us, but the school is

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: —Urgh!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Did you hear that outside?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Even a single falling rock could spell our little classroom caving in...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: But I'm not scared! Bwooom, bwoooom... I'm not scared of them!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Shut it, not a word! Lady Golding would—

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Ah, excuse me, er...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Hello, Molly. I'm a friend of Golding.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I remember now, Lady Heidi... but I'm sorry, I'll have to ask you to leave.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Wait. Why?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: If you wanted Lady Golding, she's been out of the school lately. I'm not sure where it is she's fled to, actually.

spans.text: If you wanted Lady Golding, she's been out of the school lately. I'm not sure where it

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I don't mean this against you, but... as you see, everyone's in crisis now. I don't want anyone inviting more danger upon the schoolchildren.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Did I frighten you, perhaps? You seem very out of sorts.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Ah, do I...? No, it wasn't you.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It's just, so much has happened lately. How could one not be on edge?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I really don't know how I'm even meant to protect these children, coping by myself...

spans.text: I really don't know how I'm even
to protect these children, coping by myself...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, Molly.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: If the Sarkaz do come knocking, then be forthcoming. Tell them I'm here.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: You ARE in their sights, then?!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Please, let me shelter inside for a spell. If that's okay?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I don't know... What happened to you?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I am a friend of Golding's... if that explains anything.

spans.text: a friend of Golding's... if that explains anything.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: To my mind, there's one place to hide within the school. Lady Golding didn't want me letting any old passerby know, but, well, you're no passerby.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Leo, take Lady Heidi to the underground 'storehouse', would you?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I'll stay here and wait. If Sarkaz soldiers do barge in, I'll... I'll find some way or other.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Leo, may I ask you a few questions?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Go on, ask.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: What kind of place is this underground 'storehouse'?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: You'll know it when you see it.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Is it a refuge connecting to the sewers?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: ...Who even are you?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: A friend of Miss Golding's from the literary circles, that's all.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: No need to be so astonished. After all, I've heard more than plenty about this school, and the children she taught.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Still... did Molly never actually tell you all that it's... not safe down there anymore?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Haven't heard anything like that. My family and a bunch of others too, they're all hiding in there.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (Does Molly really have no clue about the Self-Salvation Corps' retreat? Or could it be...)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Well, then, has Miss Molly seemed strange in any way, as of recent?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Strange? Nah, no way. You don't get to say mean things about her.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: But... there's some things about her that we can't really figure out.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: She's there every day, always fussing over us, and going on and on at us all the time, but then one day she suddenly ran to us and said she'd been cooped up by the Sarkaz for days on end, and thank god we're okay, and stuff.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: And ever since then she's always been all nervy, like she had a nightmare, and it's scared her stiff.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (The Damazti.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (I was only speculating at first. This place was one of the leaks in the Corps' intelligence network, so I suspected Molly had turned traitor, but now...)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (If the Damazti's found its way in, then... could even the boy before me be one of its transformations?)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (No, even if there was no sign of that shapeshifter, I'd... suspect them all anyway.)

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Hey! Where are you going?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Didn't you hear what Miss Molly said? You've got to go into the basement, down the stairs. That's the wrong way.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Listen to me, Leo.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Could you do me a favor, and let me take a walk around school on my own? You can go back and tell Miss Molly that I'm sheltered well now.
Saying so, Heidi carefully observes how he reacts.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: No, you're fibbing.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Unless you help me with a thing, too.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: What might that be?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: I want to do this ruddy Sarkaz in, but everyone says I can't go.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Humph! How come he gets to be so mean!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Uncle Jack lives in the alley over there, he's really nice, but then that Sarkaz gave him a beating, and locked him up, and it's been days now.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: I saw through a crack in the window, his arms and legs all bent into this shape. It must be horrible being twisted like that. I wanna get him free.
The child's expression remains clear, unadulterated. Heidi knows; if he was the Damazti, he'd have no need to make up this lie for himself.

spans.text: The child's expression remains clear, unadulterated. Heidi knows; if he
the Damazti, he'd have no need to make up this lie for himself.

steps.text: But she does wish to herself, for an instant, that this was not the true student of Golding, the eleven-year-old boy.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: No. Assaulting a Sarkaz would only be asking for further trouble, you understand.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: And, well... I presume this Uncle Jack you mention was left there with his limbs broken; he must have... long breathed his last.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I could explain to you the kind of brute violence the Sarkaz dole out to civilians, and why we have to endure, to protect ourselves, but...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Doesn't matter.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: If you're not going, forget it.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You're right... Explaining it doesn't matter.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: I'm not stupid. I figured that much.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: I just hate it, it feels horrible. Uncle Jack like that, I keep seeing it.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (If Golding were here, I'm sure she would pained so to see the children in this state.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (But... she at least taught them, for when tragedy visits them, to hold onto their sense of pain.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Leo.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: To tell the truth, I'm... here to check on where Golding used to live.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: There's no need to hide it. I've heard the news of her death.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: When she wasn't holding your lessons, where would she usually be?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Um, the bookshop, and the corridors if they were sunny... and, right, she had an office.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: But she didn't stay inside there much. And it was always locked, too, when she was in and when she was out.

spans.text: But she didn't stay inside there much. And it was always locked, too, when she was in

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Hm... Is it the room over that way?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Did she tell you about it?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: She's described to me, many a time, the scene one can peek through the cracks in the closed shutters. She said a broken lamppost stood outside the window. Damaged by a Sarkaz at some point, and nobody dared to go touch it.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Oh, okay. Well, anyway, it's locked—

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: —That's smoke, isn't it?!

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Where would the fire be?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: No, wait, it's a signal. There's Sarkaz coming close to the 'storehouse'.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes, this happens with the school's basement. Lt. Colonel Lettou realized as much long ago.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Is someone down there? No, they can't be. Who would come out to a place like this?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Even back when the school still had plenty of students, a long while ago, you see, we'd throw any odds and ends we had no place to keep down there. Scrap catching itself on fire has, well, happened more than once in the school's history.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: That's why you smelled smoke. I thought something wasn't right about the air either, so I came down to check.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (She's... trembling. But she's still keeping the students away, all by herself.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (Maybe I was just apprehensive, and she's innocent after all.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (Lettou's Sarkaz aren't too obedient to him, and wouldn't trust her either.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: (She just glanced that way. That's where the others should be concealed.)

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Leo, can you trust me now? Would you like to try taking down that Sarkaz a different way?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: We'll try and lure them all off.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Thank you for saving us all!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Oh, you're hurt...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: That's fine, just a little trickle—anything to get out of that rubble and scrap metal faster. We're lucky Leo isn't hurt.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: ...Lady Heidi?! Why are you pointing your cane at me?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Don't be too nervous; I just want to ask you one simple question. If you answer correctly, I'll be convinced of your trustworthiness.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: What was the first thing Clovisia ever said to you?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: What...? I don't recall this name, I'm not sure who you're telling me about, I'm sorry...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: That's alright, Molly, thank you.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I apologize—when I told you I was being tailed before, that was just a lie meant to feel you out...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Now I trust that you still love every child of this school, as you always earnestly have.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Also, you are completely unaware of the changes that transpired in this time.

spans.text: completely unaware of the changes that transpired in this time.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: In this time... You're right, yes. I've missed a great deal.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Listen to me. The Victorians that used to be active in Londinium's underground have suffered heavy losses. The Citizens' Self-Salvation Corps' network is unable to reach anybody.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Moreover, I didn't note being shadowed when I came, but the Sarkaz have appeared here.

spans.text: Moreover, I didn't note being shadowed when I came, but the Sarkaz

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I fear they've suspected this place for a while now, and Lt. Colonel Lettou's words... may not hold so much sway anymore.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It is no longer safe here. You all must find some way to relocate somewhere else.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: But where would we go?
In vain, she lifts her head and glances to the underground passage, its walls of concrete pitch-black.
She, like every other citizen trapped in Londinium, like Heidi, is left at a loss.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Please, be strong for a little while more, Molly.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: A woman once told me that it is a must, that Victorians safeguard their homeland.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I trust her. I trust that by our efforts together, we can build peace.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Haha, what a superficial piece of speech. I'm sure if Golding heard, I'd have her laughing at me again.
She knows she hasn't convinced anyone. As the crunching of a tank rumbles through the street outside, the two hang their heads low, gravely low.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I just wanted to come and see the place she lived. And... pick up a letter she'd stowed there.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: So you know she's...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Mm.
The din of war engulfs all language.
Molly approaches Heidi, stands on faint tiptoes, and wraps her tightly in a hug, gently patting her back.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Relaying intelligence out of both the Sarkaz and the dukes' sight is growing more dangerous of an ask, isn't it?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Your last reply hasn't even arrived in my hands, and yet here you are beating it to the punch.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Haha, quite... you're as shrewd as ever.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It's like I hardly needed to write what I did at all, let alone see you in person.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I'd be very disappointed if so, Heidi.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You tell me of how things are trending outside, update me on the Self-Salvation Corps and its supporters across each district...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: And our vision fills with all the inescapable vanity and conspiracy of the age, all the might and right. Is it beyond our eyes to see anything else, now?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...Of course not.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Then let down your hair for a bit, and take a break.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The children are out there frolicking in the street. This is when nobody enters the classroom to bother us.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...Very well.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I went looking per the leads you provided, but there's still no word from Ross.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The situation in Sudean has ratcheted even tighter; I have to return there after. Do you remember the name 'Rhodes Island'? They'll reach Londinium very soon...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, that all just bubbled up from somewhere.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: That's alright. You go on. I know the responsibility you're shouldering.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You said before that if anything happened to you, you might need me to handle some intelligence work in your place. Even now, I'm not sure whether I'd be able to...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: No, no, Golding, let's talk of something else.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Say—would you like to go to the theater?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Right now?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Sometime.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Once... all this is over, and Victoria rings in peaceful days again.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: When we're not performers acting out this life, nor authors wracking our brains to slip our messages through the cracks.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: When we're just normal people in the audience, moved purely by the developments of a play, free from the terror of all the rumors offstage.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: We'll give each actor a bouquet in their spitting image, just like we used to—I've always felt those bouquets really complemented you.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Of course... Yes, why not.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But... when will we find ourselves, once all this is over?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Why are you always waiting...? And what makes you so able to wait?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...Golding.
An unsent letter rests where it was placed, there on a dusty desk.
'Heidi, how do I break the children free from this age of violence? And how do I break free from it myself?'
'Oh, we impotent, defenseless book-lovers.'
'In this age where rationality and humanity have given way, whose follower should I be?'
That teacher who so loved to correspond in red pen as a joke, in her final letter, used a soft, plaintive black ink to write of her despair.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Heidi, there are times I see you looking so far ahead.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: It's hardly that I distrust you. I trust peace will come eventually.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But then, when I try to look as far as you do, all I see is the next war, grinding the facade of peace to dust.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You always seem to catch sight of some distant star, some unshakable faith.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...Nail on the head as always, Golding.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I'm just... following after the cleric we all so respected.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It was her who gave me courage. It was as if she'd seen war, seen ruin, time after countless time... it was as if she knew we could one day be past all this suffering.

spans.text: It was her who gave me courage. It was as if she'd
ruin, time after countless time... it was as if she
we could one day be past all this suffering.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Mm. You've always been her follower. You can see her light.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But I can't.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: So to my mind, the best I can do is to see what's in front of me, to trust in the here and now. So it goes for the vast majority.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: To trust our every class and play can educate the children, to trust in the little kindnesses we do the Self-Salvation Corps. It's better than cold selfishness, than a rudderless drive.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I... want to trust that what our lives are now is still worth something, just as I trust in you.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You can trust in me, Golding. You can write of this all in a letter, so I might remember for you too.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: In that case, supposing I forget one day, you must make it in time to remind me. Deal?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: She'd long... arranged a Messenger to hand me an office key.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I couldn't make it.
Countless letters and clippings still fill the deskside suitcase. They are all that's left. Heidi needs not read, for they were all sent by herself.
She came here to find again the true, inner feelings she'd divulged all those years ago.
She said as much to Golding: If I forget the grief and the roars I take down in my letters, then please, remind me.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier A
steps.text: You catch the guys from today?

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier B
steps.text: Missed 'em.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier B
steps.text: They'll all be stuck before long, anyway.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier A
steps.text: Hah, true. No place to run. Those poor insects ain't ever seen what war really is.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier A
steps.text: —What's that?
The two Sarkaz soldiers assigned to night patrol look up.
From atop a skyscraper's ruins come pieces of paper, floating down.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier B
steps.text: That's a lotta writing.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier A
steps.text: Is each one the same?

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier B
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Patrolling Sarkaz Soldier A
steps.text: Then who cares. Someone's just tossing out their wastebasket.
The Sarkaz tosses the letter paper to the ground, and gives it a few stamps underfoot.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: What a waste for you to throw these letters away... and how dangerous.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: That's alright. Our correspondence was never a signed one.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: And besides, they were just letters from me to Golding... odd essays and nothing more.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: She always liked to joke to me that since I'd be going my whole life in the guise of a third-rate novelist, covering for my intel gathering work...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I may well be waiting until after my death to get the fame I deserve, when all these private letters can be published.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: So here we are... isn't this publishing, in a way?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I understand her choice. I understand how she couldn't bear this age any longer, just how despair and estrangement and hatred overwhelmed her.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Wounded compatriots unwilling to rise again, friends forced to suspect one another, children tasting suffering and hostility in the first years of their lives.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: How such stories are so omnipresent, yet so unspeakable.
Depression. Sorrow. Indignity. Loathing. Penetrating critiques and satires, desperately longed-for images and memories.
Everything she endured. Everything she waited for.
The letters tell all across the dark street floor.
To the city, she lets out silent howl after howl.
But she's fully aware that no one will pick them up from the flagstone street slicked in engine oil, let alone discern the handwriting.
All falls still again. The only sound Londinium produces in return, the day-and-night rumble of the military factories, somewhere close by.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...And how powerless these words I play around with are.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: No more will there be letters.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: But, you know—I still feel it's a waste of sorts...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: When Lady Golding put on plays for the children, she'd always bring up the suggestions you made for them in your letters, and how they always hit where it hurt.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Heidi, will you ever... still write your own thoughts, the way you did in those?
Back, to the ground, all the paper falls.

a.text: You always say if the writing's gone poorly, it's fine to tear up the work. In that light, you'll surely approve of my act of casting away those old letters.
I've come to realize that my unconditional trust—and pursuit—of such a distant ideal is hardly a promised path, hardly bound to just come about under her witness with a finger's snap.
And the calls I once penned from behind as I followed in her tracks; those were no full answer to the lives we have now.
This new life suffused in torment, from my confusion and my loss, from my own soul-searching. Something tells me—that I should be more than just a follower.
This is... the first letter I write you. By my finite insight, by my frail and fleeting life, I want to press on ahead with others, and perhaps, come some time or other, I'll become a leader.
Oh, how I wish my critic could be not the ruthless present, but you instead.
